A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Raw2Drive and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Their content can be reliably matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Raw2Drive results on CARLA Leaderboard 2.0 and Bench2Drive, component ablations, training-loss curves, and qualitative reconstructions.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds spatial/temporal alignment ablation results and measurements of inference latency.

M1.justification: The dual-stream architecture, rollout and head guidance, shared stochastic sampling, losses, and two-stage training algorithm are retained. The new alignment ablation tests existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions use CARLA 0.9.15.1, Leaderboard 2.0 validation/devtest routes, Bench2Drive, and Dev10. The added analyses introduce no new dataset, driving task, sensor environment, or population.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain identical comparator membership, including the privileged Think2Drive expert and the same IL methods. The added studies concern internal alignment variants and the two existing streams; newly cited works are not added benchmark baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a four-condition spatial/temporal alignment experiment on Dev10 and module-level latency evaluation in milliseconds. Existing route selections, training budgets, and driving metrics remain unchanged. Hardware and timing procedures for the latency measurements are not specified.

E4.justification: New Table 8 separately disables spatial and temporal alignment to examine their contributions. Appendix G adds a latency breakdown to identify computational bottlenecks. Earlier component ablations, convergence analysis, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that Dev10 ablations are repeated three times and averaged. v2 adds no seed disclosure, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports spatial-only DS 13.6 and SR 1.2/10, and temporal-only DS 9.24 and SR 0.8/10. Table 13 adds encoder latencies of 600 ms for the raw stream and 2 ms for the privileged stream, with 2 ms world-model and policy entries. Matched benchmark and earlier ablation values are unchanged, including Table 5's Raw2Drive DS 71.36 and SR 50.24%.

T1.justification: The state definitions, alignment objective, world-model losses, and actor-critic equations are unchanged in Table 2, Section 3.3, and Appendices B–E. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal novelty, performance, and training-cost claims are retained. However, v2's conclusion removes v1's explicit claim that privileged guidance applies to any sensor beyond camera-only systems, modestly narrowing the stated applicability.

C2.justification: v2 identifies the vision encoder as the latency bottleneck and adds an argument that the design is conceptually decoupled from the simulator, replacing v1's future-work statement about policy-training guidance. It also removes the caveat about unverified industry training practices and changes potential social-impact benefits into affirmative safety and generalization statements.

D1.justification: Table 13 newly describes the privileged encoder as 5×Conv. v2 removes Appendix G.4's pointer to Raw2Drive.mov, without establishing that the video itself became unavailable. Training hyperparameters, action definitions, and GPU-day disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including UniZero, RAT, DriveMoE, ReSim, and several additional RL works, largely through citation clusters in existing passages. The substantive positioning relative to imitation learning, model-free RL, and privileged-input MBRL remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and typo corrections, updates author affiliations and conference text, and renames the existing rollout ablation subsection. Limitations and social impact move from Appendix G.3 into Section 5; the main narrative remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8 and 13, places the parameter-sharing and policy-finetuning tables side by side, and relocates the notation table and several figures. Existing diagrams, loss curves, and qualitative panels retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added alignment ablation provides more direct support for an existing design choice, while Table 13 makes the substantial vision-encoder latency visible. These improve empirical support and practical transparency without changing the main benchmark evidence. Unspecified timing conditions and more categorical social-impact wording without corresponding new validation temper the gains.
